html:
The Qatar diplomatic crisis began on 5 June 2017, when Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain and Egypt cut ties with Qatar and closed their borders, air space and ports to it.

They accused Qatar of backing Islamist groups and of being too close to Iran, and they demanded that it shut down Al Jazeera. Qatar refused. Its only land border, with Saudi Arabia, was closed, so food came in by air and sea from Turkey and Iran, and it built up its own dairy farms almost overnight.

The blockade ended with the Al-Ula declaration in January 2021. Qatar came out of it with its policies unchanged and its gas wealth intact, which let it host the World Cup the next year.
sum: The Qatar diplomatic crisis began on 5 June 2017, when Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain and Egypt cut ties with Qatar and closed their borders, air space and ports to it.
